Chief_Complaint.content: Patient reports feeling really anxious for approximately 2 months.
Anxiety has worsened with new job.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: For approximately 2 months the patient has been feeling really anxious, worsened with a new job, associated with palpitations and poor sleep.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: CC: “feeling really anxious” x ~2 mo; worsened with new job; palpitations; poor sleep

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient experiences morning dread about leaving the house.
Patient has work-focused anxiety and reports that her boss is unkind.
Patient goes to bed between 22:00 and 23:00 but takes a long time to fall asleep.
Patient reports shallow sleep of about 3–4 hours per night.
Patient wakes before the alarm with palpitations and a racing heart.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: wakes before alarm with palpitations; heart “racing,”

History_of_Present_Illness.content: On one occasion the patient feared she was having a heart attack due to palpitations.
Palpitations are irregular and last minutes up to about 10 minutes.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Palpitations: irregular; lasts mins up to ~10 min

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports no chest pain, only discomfort when the heart is beating fast.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: no chest pain (only discomfort when fast)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: During the daytime the patient has very low energy, anhedonia, and feels on edge but continues to attend work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Daytime: very low energy; anhedonia; on edge; continues to attend work

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient avoids going out and has reduced contact with friends.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Social: avoids going out; reduced contact with friends

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has stopped running and playing tennis.
Work stress is a trigger for the patient’s symptoms.
Public transport, especially the tube when it is hot and airless, triggers symptoms.
Patient’s mood is persistently down.
Patient denies any prior similar episode of low mood or anxiety.
Patient denies panic attacks but is worried that it is building up.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Denies panic attacks; worried it’s building up

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies suicidal ideation and reports good family support.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Denies SI; has good family support

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient’s appetite is unchanged and she is eating regularly.
Patient reports increased chocolate intake.
Patient has previously spoken with her mother about her symptoms.
Patient has had no prior therapy.
Patient is open to one-to-one therapy.

Family_History.content: Patient’s mother has a history of past depression.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks heavily on Friday and Saturday, exceeding recommended limits.
Patient drinks approximately one glass of wine during the week.

Assessment.content: Work-related anxiety with insomnia, palpitations, low mood, and anhedonia; no suicidal ideation.
Assessment.source_text: 1) Work-related anxiety with insomnia and palpitations; low mood/anhedonia; no SI

Assessment.content: Palpitations are likely anxiety-related, with irregular, brief episodes and no chest pain.
Assessment.source_text: 2) Palpitations likely anxiety-related; irregular, brief episodes; no chest pain

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to self-refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT); link to be sent.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT); link to be sent

Plan_of_Care.content: Add sleep hygiene advice to the notes.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: add sleep hygiene advice to notes

Plan_of_Care.content: Order basic blood tests to assess for triggers of palpitations as requested by GP.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Basic blood tests to assess for triggers of palpitations (per GP request)

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to call support line to arrange blood tests.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Patient to call support line to arrange blood tests

Plan_of_Care.content: Safety net advice: call back if symptoms are worsening, if unable to cope with work or activities of daily living, or if therapies are not helping.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety net: call back if worsening, unable to cope with work/ADLs, or therapies not helping

Plan_of_Care.content: Medications are not first line; consider medication if there is no improvement or deterioration.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Meds: not 1st line; consider if no improvement or deterioration

Follow_up_Information.content: GP follow-up planned 1 week after blood tests to review results.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: GP F/U 1 week after bloods to review results

Physical_Findings.content: No vitals or physical examination findings documented.
